Increase the carved void so it reads as a usable open-space figure rather than a narrow separation gap.
Open the courtyard toward the verified access side to align the public threshold with the street edge.
Add a section-defining support layer to improve roof/section fit for neighborhood living while keeping the courtyard mass primary.
Give the upper mass a calm shed section compatible with the portfolio slot and mixed-use neighborhood brief.
Align the shed section with the long axis to preserve a coherent dominant gesture and strengthen sectional continuity.

graph_edits.rationale: Retarget the dominant mass from a simple split-wing separation to a courtyard-based public figure so the form can support a clearer neighborhood threshold and usable open space.
Carve a more legible central void with enough breadth to read as public rather than merely as a split seam.
Align the public opening to the site access side in the program frame so the street edge becomes an active threshold.
Introduce a section-active support condition to break the boxy roofline and create a clearer public/upper hierarchy without erasing the dominant mass.
Use a shed-profile section to support the neighborhood brief and give the mass a readable top-side orientation.
Orient the profiled section along the long axis to reinforce the existing compact-bar logic while improving sectional clarity.

rationale: The candidate reads as a coherent early massing in all views, but the dominant move is still a generic split box with a shallow puncture rather than a convincing neighborhood-living building. The parcel is respected in a basic sense, but the form responds weakly to it: the mass fills the site as two blunt volumes with only a narrow internal gap, so the open-space figure is not yet clearly public or spatially generous. The blue frontage edge is not actively answered; there is no strong court, notch, undercut, or entry seam aligned to the access edge, so the street threshold remains semantically passive. In section, the object is box-like and low-relief, lacking a legible roof/section idea, terrace logic, or a ground-enhancing cut that would support mixed-use neighborhood life. The form has reasonable repair integrity and does not appear self-colliding across views, but it is too typologically generic relative to the brief and references.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: More expressive roof curvature and pavilion-like openness than the candidate; candidate is boxier and less civic at ground.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Three-part low-rise massing with a central void and upper bridge reads as a community-oriented public threshold.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Much larger and more campus-like; not a direct typological match for this compact mass.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Courtyard/plaza-centered campus logic with stepped low-rise components can organize neighborhood program.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference is a more resolved public civic object; candidate lacks comparable carving and entry emphasis.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A recessed void and overhanging upper mass create a legible public threshold at the street edge.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Candidate does not yet express the horizontal spread or roof profile that carries this principle.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Elongated low-rise spread with a central void and a gently sloped roof suggests active neighborhood mixed-use.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Candidate is closer to split blocks than to a truly terraced, connective section; void logic is underdeveloped.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Multiple wings around a central courtyard with connecting bridges and terraced section supports neighborhood-community use well.

warnings: Parcel containment appears acceptable in the visible views, but the form is still judged weak on program semantics.
The access edge is not clearly activated; no strong public void reads as addressing the verified frontage.
The current split-wing language is visible but under-structured; the gap behaves more like separation than public space.
